svg.text: OpenGrid Orchestrator — Power Quality: Waveform to Physical Swap
MVP-S+ (06-service-profiles-and-power-quality.md). BUILT/LIVE/PLANNED via grep on main @ f3b3365. Wave 2 ingestion + guardian checks are now LIVE; asset-health orchestration is built, 0 callers.
built + wired (live)
built in ogsim, not MQTT-wired
schema only (migration exists, unpopulated)
planned — no code
1. Hub inverter model + waveform generation (WP-H)
ogsim.fleet.{pq,wave} — LIVE: characterization + real sample synthesis
BUILT: one InverterUnit per hub (two for a dual-unit home) with freq/voltage offsets, THD_I,
3rd/5th/7th harmonics, phase_angle_error, quality_score; ambient Ornstein-Uhlenbeck drift every
tick; PQ anomaly catalogue (frequency_drift, harmonic_injection, phase_imbalance_injection,
calibration_drift_correctable/hardware) injectable via scenario/cmd (LIVE end-to-end).
LIVE (WP-H, 9153dc2): ogsim.fleet.wave, a module separate from pq.py (its brief: “call pq's
access function, don't edit it”). synthesize_raw_capture() (wave.py:282) builds real v(t)/i(t)
sample arrays from S7.4's sinusoid-plus-dominant-harmonics model, quantized to int16;
build_summary_message() (wave.py:184) builds the periodic summary. runtime.FleetEngine publishes
summaries through a 10 s default gate, raw captures from a 1 %/min RotatingAuditSampler
(runtime.py:170-186, 454-455), and answers an inbound .../request (__main__.py:113-123).
pq.py's “never generates samples itself” docstring refers to pq.py alone.
og/v1/scada/wave/.../summary|raw — LIVE; .../request — ogsim ready, nothing triggers one yet
2. SCADA wave transport → ingestion → storage
opengrid.pq_ingest (NEW, 9153dc2) · engine-owned, wired into og-engine
LIVE: og-engine's _mqtt_ingest_loop subscribes scada/wave/+/+/+/summary and .../raw. Summaries
buffer in memory (_pending_summaries) and flush as ONE batched executemany on [pq_ingest].
flush_interval_s (default 2 s) or at flush_batch_size — fixing a per-message-commit that stalled
the SCADA write path at ~1,000 msg/s (S9 build report). Raw captures validate+blob-write in a
background worker (engine.background.BackgroundIngest, aa8a2d3/d2c57b7) off the ingest loop —
~34% of og-engine CPU moved off the event loop (live 2026-09-26). ogsim's own summary gate
(WaveConfig.summary_interval_s) defaults to 10 s. og.pq_waveform_summary/_raw_index both write.
per-phase measurement
3. Envelope checks — WARN / BREACH hysteresis (K14)
opengrid.core.pq.envelope — pure math, built
BUILT: evaluate_envelope (per-dimension NOMINAL/WARN/BREACH at 70%/100% of the
PowerQualityEnvelope limit) and step_hysteresis (asymmetric dwell: WARN/BREACH commit only
after sustaining past a candidate window; recovery needs < 60% — the same dwell pattern as the
$5/MWh price-response switch, diagram 02). Called by tests and nothing else in production.
LIVE (NEW, 9153dc2): guardian/pq_checks.py's G-21 (per-phase imbalance) / G-22 (THD) / G-23
(freq/voltage deviation) / G-24 (ride-through, asset-state conformance) / G-25 (calibration
safety) — additive to checks.py, called from service.py's _check_power_quality(), which
guardian's evaluate_and_sign() ALREADY calls into its violations list (same path as every
other G-check). guardian/pq_repo.py's Postgres ports (envelope limits, measured/modelled
measurement fallback, asset-state, calibration history) are wired via repo.build_pg_ports().
G-21..G-23 only run when an obligation behind the bank carries a non-default PQ envelope.
Allocator PQ-aware selection/continuous monitoring is a SEPARATE, still-unbuilt gap: grep
"pq"/"PQ" across opengrid.allocator — still 0 files reference it at all.
on a sustained BREACH
4. Corrective ladder
rebalance → substitute → recalibrate → reactive/PF → exclude
PLANNED end to end: no controller code sequences this ladder anywhere. Two of its steps have
real math sitting unused, ready for a future controller to call:
• substitution: the SAME allocator.realize_obligation() diagram 02 already runs every 2 s for
unhealthy hubs — reusable, but nothing triggers it FROM a PQ breach today.
• remote recalibration: MORE built now (9153dc2), still not connected end to end. Guardian
G-25 exists and gates signing (guardian.pq_checks.check_g25_calibration_safety, wired into
service.evaluate_and_sign_calibration()). opengrid.assets.AssetHealthService.request_
calibration() can build a bounded CalibrationCandidate from a drift observation. But grep
finds 0 production callers of AssetHealthService anywhere (engine/guardian/settle/api) —
nothing ever calls request_calibration() then hands the result to the guardian to sign, and
no MQTT code publishes cmd/cal/<hub> or subscribes ack/cal/<hub> on either side (grep: 0 hits,
both directions, unchanged this round). ogsim.fleet.calibration.apply_calibration (hub side)
is likewise unit-tested and unreachable in production.
Rebalance, reactive/PF adjustment and exclusion (removing a hub from PQ-sensitive selection):
no code at all — not even a stub.
ladder exhausted / hardware fault
5. Asset health
opengrid.assets (NEW, 9153dc2) — fully coded, zero production callers
BUILT, much more than schema now: opengrid.assets.state_machine (pure OK→WATCH→DEGRADED→
QUARANTINED→AWAITING_REPLACEMENT→RECOMMISSIONING→OK, fail-closed on any other event) and
AssetHealthService (evaluate_drift, request_calibration, record_calibration_result, quarantine,
open_work_order, schedule_replacement, record_inverter_replaced, verify_recommissioning — every
transition traced K10/K11). assets.repo has real Postgres ports (PgAssetHealthRepo etc.).
Still PLANNED: nothing calls AssetHealthService (grep: 0 hits in engine/guardian/settle/api).
asset_state never changes outside a test — every hub reads its schema default 'OK' in
production. The gap is the missing scheduler/caller, not the guardian (its G-25/pq_repo half
is already wired — see stage 3/4).
QUARANTINED / AWAITING_REPLACEMENT
6. Maintenance work order
og.maintenance_work_order — migrations/0011, schema only
BUILT: work_order_id, severity, evidence (jsonb), status (OPEN/IN_PROGRESS/CLOSED/CANCELLED);
AssetHealthService.open_work_order() (NEW) would insert one. PLANNED: nothing calls it (same
0-caller gap as stage 5) — no row exists on this checkout.
technician dispatched (manual, outside this repo)
7. Physical inverter swap / recommissioning
ogsim.fleet.pq.replace_inverter() — LIVE as a manual scenario action
BUILT and LIVE: the "replace_inverter" scenario-control catalogue entry (control/catalogue.py,
wire_type FLEET_REPLACE_INVERTER, owner=fleet, target=hub) — an operator/scenario-YAML
action published on scenario/cmd reaches ogsim.fleet.runtime.handle_scenario_cmd, which calls
replace_inverter(): resets the hub's offsets to a freshly-drawn “new unit”, records new
serial/firmware, clears any active calibration-drift anomaly.
PLANNED: nothing AUTOMATIC triggers this from asset-health degradation (stage 5 never runs).
AssetHealthService.record_inverter_replaced() (NEW) would write an og.asset_event row
(event_type INVERTER_REPLACED) and advance asset_state to RECOMMISSIONING — but ogsim (this
scenario action) and the orchestrator's assets package are separate deployables with no call
path between them, so this still never fires on this checkout (same 0-caller gap as stage 5).

calibration-command safety (bounds,

All five: LIVE (NEW, 9153dc2) via guardian/pq_checks.py + pq_repo.py
Terminology (BUILD.md §2a.4, NOTICES.md)
“Substitution” = software move of delivery
between hubs (diagram 02/03, R-SUBSTITUTION).
“Inverter swap / replacement” = physical
hardware action (stage 7 above).
“Recalibration” is tried remotely first.
